title: Campo: the design round — paper, forest and rust, serif stems, a bottom tab bar; merged to main and deployed
description:
The Caçador app restyled to design direction 1, "Campo": a field notebook on a warm paper ground with ink text, forest green as the working colour and rust for the one thing to do next, Fraunces for the stems and the numbers over Source Sans 3 for everything else, and a bottom tab bar as the menu. Ross chose it on 2026-10-14 over the two other directions on the design canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/Hw7LgYnu3QzndKq2AJyEvt, row 1) and asked for no discussion: build it, merge it straight into main and push, so GitHub Pages serves it at once.

Plan: DESIGN.md § 6.3 (Home and the menu), § 8.1 (layout), § 8.2 (routes), § 8.5 (look), § 8.6 (the question card), § 9 (decision record), all as bead .1 rewrites them; the design reference in design/campo/ (the five Campo artboards and a README; untracked in the main checkout until .1 adds them). The behaviour rules of DESIGN.md § 6 and § 7 stand unchanged except where DECISIONS names an addition.

IN SCOPE: apps/web restyled on every screen (Home, Practice with the question card, Exam start, running and results, Progress, Settings, Flagged, not-found); the two fonts self-hosted and precached; the light and dark token sets; the bottom tab bar and the screen header with the back control; three small additions the chosen artboards carry (Weakest topics on Home, the answered count on the exam-in-progress card, the unanswered count on Submit); the e2e suite updated to the new look; DESIGN.md and CLAUDE.md updated; pnpm lint, pnpm test and pnpm e2e green; the epic merged into main and pushed, the deploy workflow green, the live site checked.
OUT OF SCOPE: any other behaviour change; packages/data; the app icon and manifest (the Ç mark stays); a dark-mode toggle (the system setting decides, as before); a pull request or a recording; the two rejected directions.
notes:
**DECISIONS** (epic-scoped log; durable record written to DESIGN.md § 6.3, § 8.1, § 8.2, § 8.5, § 8.6 and § 9 in bead .1)

• D1 Direction: Campo (Ross, 2026-10-14, over Alvo and Azulejo on the design canvas, row 1; the reference files are design/campo/). The look is a field notebook: a warm paper ground, ink text, forest for the working colour (tabs, right answers, bars), rust for the one thing to do next and for a wrong answer, hairlines and plates, no shadows. The paper ground is the one cream the app allows, by Ross's choice. Supersedes cac-eil D7's neutral base. Reason: Ross found the neutral app "not something I would want to use".
• D2 Tokens, light: paper #F4F0E6 (the ground), card #FBF8F1, line #D9D2C2, track #E6E0D2, ink #1C2620, muted #5A6256, eyebrow #4F6650, forest #2E5A3A, moss tint #DDE8DA, moss line #B9C9B6, rust #B5461C, clay tint #F3DED2; text on a forest or rust fill is card. Dark: ground #151A17, card #1C2320, line #33403A, track #2A332D, ink #EDE8DB, muted #B3BAAE, eyebrow #9DBAA2, forest #7FB58C, moss tint #243A2C, moss line #3A5543, rust #E0784F, clay tint #3E2419; text on a forest or rust fill is the ground. Every text colour on its ground passes 4.5:1 (3:1 at 24 px and above) as listed; a worker who changes a value checks it. The shadcn tokens map onto these: background paper, card, border line, foreground ink, muted-foreground muted, primary rust, secondary card with the ink hairline, accent moss tint, destructive rust, success forest, ring forest; dark stays keyed on prefers-color-scheme, never a class (cac-eil D7 kept). Reason: the canvas's style tile, checked for contrast.
• D3 Type: Fraunces, variable with the opsz and wght axes, weight 600, for the app name, screen titles, the question stem, every number that is the point of its screen (readiness, the clock, percentages, scores, the day counts) and the option letters; Source Sans 3, variable wght, for everything else: body 16 to 17 px, secondary 13 to 14 px, eyebrows 12 px uppercase with 0.14em tracking at 600. Both self-hosted from @fontsource-variable/fraunces and @fontsource-variable/source-sans-3 (installed under the three-day rule, the previous version when the newest is too new), upright only, latin and latin-ext subsets only, declared by the app's own @font-face rules under the family names "Fraunces" and "Source Sans 3" with font-display swap over the system stack, so the build carries exactly four woff2 files (about 220 KB) and all four are in the precache: the fonts work offline and never flash to a fallback after the first visit. Google Fonts is never linked. Reverses cac-eil D7 "system font stack, no web fonts". Reason: the serif is the look; offline is a product rule (DESIGN.md § 8.8).
• D4 Shape: corners 6 px (chips, markers, badges), 8 px (controls and rows), 10 px (cards and plates); 1 px hairlines in the line colour; no shadows, no gradients; every touch target at least 44 px; the page gutter 20 px; the column stays phone-first and max-w-2xl. The named exclusions stand: no pill buttons, no "01 / 02 / 03" section labels, no italic accent words, no gradient hero, no chart library. Icons are lucide (already a dependency): house, target, timer, chart-no-axes-column, sliders-horizontal, flag, languages, lightbulb, check, x, chevron-right, arrow-left; stroke 1.75, never emoji. Reason: the style tile.
• D5 Menu: a bottom tab bar with four tabs, Home, Practice, Exam and Progress (labels from common.nav, so no new common strings; icons house, target, timer, chart-no-axes-column; the current tab in forest with a filled icon and aria-current="page"), on every screen except the /exam route (the start screen and the running exam take the whole screen and keep the back control only); the results route, Settings, Flagged and not-found show the bar with no tab current. Settings is reached from a control on Home's header (icon sliders-horizontal, accessible name "Settings") and Flagged from Progress and Settings as now. The back control to Home stays on every screen but Home, as a left arrow at the start of the screen header, accessible name unchanged ("Back to Home"). Tab links are named exactly the nav words; Home's two cards carry a longer accessible name (the title plus its line), so an exact "Practice" or "Exam" link query finds the tab only. Reverses cac-eil D19 "no bottom bar". Reason: Ross asked for "a decent menu system"; four destinations fit a tab bar.
• D6 Screen header: every screen but Home opens with one row: the back control, then an eyebrow (the section · topic on Practice, the screen name elsewhere) over a line in Fraunces 16 px muted (the question number on Practice, "n of 20" on the exam, "N % · M unseen" on Progress), and a right-hand slot (the clock on the exam). Home's header is the app name in Fraunces 34 px with the Settings control at the right. Bead .3 lands the header and the tab bar as shared pieces under apps/web/src/components/nav/; each screen renders the header itself, so a screen's own data can sit in it. Reason: the canvas.
• D7 Home: the readiness plate (card, hairline, 10 px; eyebrow "Readiness"; the percentage in Fraunces 64 px; the unseen count beside it in muted; a forest bar on the track with a rust tick at 75 % and "Pass line 75 %" in rust under it); the exam-in-progress card in clay with a rust hairline, the timer icon, "Exam in progress" and under it "N minutes left · A of 20 answered" (the answered count is new; A from the exam's answers); two cards side by side, Practice (rust fill, card text, target icon, line "Weak ones first") and Exam (card with an ink hairline, timer icon, line "20 questions · 30 min", the numbers from the model); then "Weakest topics" (new): an eyebrow with an "All topics" link to Progress at the right, and the two lowest started topics by group accuracy in Progress's worst-first order, each a card row with the name, "Seen x of y" and the percentage in Fraunces 22 px (rust under 75, forest at 75 or above), linking to focused practice on that topic; one row when one topic is started; the section absent while none is (a fresh device shows no section). The four buttons of cac-eil D11 are replaced by the two cards plus the tab bar. Reason: the Home artboard; the weakest rows make Home the place to start.
• D8 Practice and the question card: the picture sits whole on a plate (card, 8 px padding, hairline, 10 px corners), centred, at most 240 px tall, never cropped (the species must be identifiable; the bank's pictures are small); the stem in Fraunces 24 px; options are rows (card, hairline, 8 px) with the letter in a 28 px circle outlined in ink and Fraunces 15 px; after answering the correct row turns moss tint with a forest hairline, its letter filled forest, a tick and the word "Right"; the chosen wrong row turns clay with a rust hairline, its letter filled rust, a cross and the word "Wrong"; the exam's chosen, unrevealed row is filled ink with card text and a card-outlined letter. Under the options one row of two buttons, "Hold for English" (three fifths, card with an ink hairline, inverted to ink with card text while held, icon languages) and "Hint" (two fifths, card, hairline, icon lightbulb); the hint panel is a moss-tint block with no border, 10 px, with the eyebrows "Language notes" and "Nudge" in forest, each note's Portuguese phrase in Fraunces 600 followed by a middle dot and its English in eyebrow colour, then the note, and the nudge under a moss-line rule; the flags row reads "Report:" (new string) in muted followed by the two chips (card, hairline, 8 px, 36 px tall, flag icon); Next is a rust-filled button with a chevron. Behaviour unchanged (cac-eil D20, D23). Reason: the Practice artboard.
• D9 Exam: the start screen keeps its intro and rules on a plate with Start in rust and no tab bar; the running exam shows the header "Exam" over "n of 20" with the clock at the right in a chip (card, ink hairline, 8 px, timer icon, Fraunces 22 px tabular; the role timer and the name "Time left" as now); the markers are a 10-column grid of numbered 28 px squares with 6 px corners: answered forest with card text, current rust with card text, unanswered card with the hairline; options as D8 unrevealed; a muted centred line under them, "Answers are not marked until you submit. No English and no hints during the exam." (new string); Previous (card, ink hairline, chevron) and Next (forest fill) side by side at the bottom, Submit under them as a rust-outlined button reading "Submit · N unanswered" while N is above 0 and "Submit" otherwise (new string); the confirm dialog unchanged. Results: the score in Fraunces 64 px worded as now, "Pass mark 15", a chip Passed (moss tint, forest text) or Not passed (clay, rust text), the wrong ones on the card revealed as D8 with "Not answered" above an unanswered one; the tab bar shows with no tab current. Reason: the Exam artboard.
• D10 Progress: the header per D6 with "Progress" in Fraunces 28 px and "N % · M unseen" at the right; the 30-day plate: eyebrow "Last 30 days" with "Today: N answers, M right" at the right, bars as stacked blocks per day (the right answers in forest, the rest in the track colour, today's right block in rust) over a 1 px ink baseline, the first day's date and "Today" in rust under it; the accuracy section: eyebrow "Accuracy" with the hint "Weakest first. Tap one to practise it." at the right, underline tabs Topics, Sections, Patterns (a 2 px forest underline and bold on the open one), rows as card rows with the name, "Seen x of y" or "Not started · N questions", a 64 px mini bar and the percentage in Fraunces 20 px (rust under 75, forest otherwise, a dash and muted when not started); past exams as card rows with the date, "13 / 20" in Fraunces 20 px and a chip Passed (moss) or Not passed (clay); then the Flagged (N) link as an ink-outlined row with the flag icon and a chevron. The list rules of cac-eil D11 (29, 11, 17 rows; worst first; the open tab in the address) stand. Reason: the Progress artboard.
• D11 Settings, Flagged and not-found follow the style tile with no new layout: eyebrows for the sections (Language, Progress); the language choice as two chips with the current one filled forest; Export, Share and Import as card buttons with an ink hairline; Clear progress as a rust-outlined button; the not-saving line on a clay plate; the Flagged link as on Progress. Flagged: rows as cards with "Question N" in Fraunces, the kind as a chip, the note, the stem in muted, Clear per row; Copy in rust with Share beside it. Not-found: the title in Fraunces. Reason: the tile's rules cover them; the canvas shows no artboard for them.
• D12 Names are the contract: accessible names and roles do not change in the restyle except where a DECISION names a new string (D7's lines and section, "Report:", the exam line, "Submit · N unanswered", the answered count); new strings go into the screen's en and pt files (cac-eil D18, pt-PT); the e2e suite is updated for the named changes only, by bead .9. Exam answers are written to the answers log at Submit only (mode exam, the exam id; an unanswered question is recorded with no chosen option and correct false) and feed the practice weights like any answer. • D5 Two numbers. Readiness: for each seen question the share right in its recent list (its last three answers), an unseen question counts one third (chance on three options), the mean over all 506 shown as a rounded percentage against 75 % with the unseen count beside it (33 % and 506 unseen on a fresh device). Draw weights from the question state: unseen 3; wrong last time (attempts above 0, streak 0) 4; streak 1 → 2; streak 2 → 1; streak 3 or more → 0.5; the draw excludes the most recently drawn ids, the window being the smaller of ten and half the pool rounded down (ten for the whole bank and any pool of twenty or more, five for a pool of eleven, one for a pool of two or three, nothing for a pool of one), so the weights still act inside a small topic. Weight is computed from the state at draw time and never stored. Reason: the score rises only by covering and holding the bank, a wrong answer comes back soon without taking over (brief D5); the half-pool window because 13 of the 29 topics have eleven questions or fewer and a window of pool minus one made them a fixed rotation (Ross's default on the epic review, 2026-10-13).

title: Standing hint rulings: DESIGN.md § 5 step 3 and the pattern notes carry what the run settled
description: Outcome: a worker who writes or checks hints after this phase finds every ruling this run settled in the plan and the data, not only in the epic notes, as cac-qre did for translations (1399019). title: Phase 3: hints — pattern list, 506 hints written and checked
description:
Pointer: DESIGN.md § 3 (data layout, § 3.3 shapes), § 4 (rules 5 and 8), § 5 step 3 (pipeline), § 9 (decision record); brief cac-bc2 (description = summary with D1 to D8, notes = FOUND with the sweep counts). Hints come before the app, the order § 5 gives.

Scope in: hints/patterns.json, the closed list of constructions, with validator rule 8 checking every tag against it; one hints/en/ file per chunk file, all 506 entries, every entry at status checked by the end (hints/en/01-documentos.json already exists, hand-written in the brief as the precedent); the loader wired for all 18 files and exporting the pattern list; hint and pattern counts in pnpm validate; DESIGN.md carrying the rules; pnpm lint and pnpm test green.
Scope out: showing hints, the "hint is off" flag and status reviewed (app epic); any edit to questions/ or the extractor; translation changes beyond the fixes writers and checkers report (bead .24 applies them); hints in Portuguese; a notes field or any other change to the hint shape.
notes:
**DECISIONS** (epic-scoped log; durable record written to DESIGN.md § 3, § 4, § 5 step 3 and § 9 in bead .1)
- D1 A language note is written only for a word or construction that changes the reading of the sentence (só, desde que, não, a partir de, bem como, a false friend like única or processo), in the stem or in an option; never a vocabulary gloss the peek already gives; an empty list is right on a plain stem; at most four entries per question. Its pt is verbatim from the question or option (rule 5), its en is the wording the translation uses for that phrase, its note gives the meaning. Rule 11 carries over: a name under test is never glossed in a language note. Reason: 345 of 506 stems carry no construction and the peek covers vocabulary (brief cac-bc2 FOUND). Precedent: hints/en/01-documentos.json.
- D2 Pattern tags come from a closed list, packages/data/hints/patterns.json, an array of { slug, pt, en, note }: slug the kebab-case tag hints use, unique; pt the construction as the bank prints it or a short Portuguese label when it has no single form; en the English name the app's report shows; note what the construction does to the reading and when to tag it. Built by .3 from a sweep of the bank, about 20 entries and never more than 25; the validator (rule 8) rejects a tag that is not a slug in it. A writer who needs a tag the list lacks leaves the question untagged and reports it in the close reason for .24. Reason: the app reports accuracy per pattern, which needs a fixed vocabulary with enough questions each; the § 3.3 list does not match the bank (brief cac-bc2 D2).
- D3 The nudge is never empty, at most two sentences, states the fact behind the keyed answer and what separates a near-miss distractor, quotes the Portuguese words that carry the fact, and never names the letter; an image question's nudge gives the species' distinguishing field marks. Reason: the app already marks the correct option; the nudge's job is the fact and the contrast (brief D3).
- D4 A nudge asserts only what the bank itself and the two glossaries establish: no law citations, no article numbers, no recollection of the law beyond the keyed option. The checker narrows a nudge it cannot confirm to what the keyed option asserts. Reason: no official manual exists and nothing in the repo verifies a recollection (brief D4).
- D5 hints/en/01-documentos.json, hand-written in the brief and read by Ross, is the precedent every writer and checker reads first; it goes through .14 like any other file. Reason: brief D5.
- D6 A tag is applied only where the construction is part of what the answer turns on, not on every occurrence (in the precedent, 4 of 10 entries carry a tag; entry 3 carries none because the number decides). Reason: a low score on a pattern should mean that construction cost answers (brief D6).
- D7 A nudge may cross-reference another question by number ("question 10 asks the same with rabbits"), with the fact always stated in words too. Reason: ids are stable and the app can link them later (brief D7).

title: Phase 2: English translations — species and terms glossaries, 506 entries translated and checked
description:
Pointer: DESIGN.md § 3 (data layout, § 3.3 shapes), § 4 (rules 5 and 6), § 5 step 2 (pipeline), § 9 (decision record); brief cac-qgb (description = summary, notes = DECISIONS and the quality sample of the earlier draft).

Scope in: glossary/species.json for every species the bank names plus Portaria 67/2024's list; glossary/terms.json for the hunting and legal vocabulary; one translations/en/ file per chunk file, all 506 entries, every entry at status checked by the end; the loader hook wired; pnpm lint and pnpm test green with rules 5 and 6 live.
Scope out: hints (phase 3 epic); status reviewed and any in-app control for it (phase 4 epic); a validator rule that enforces terms in translations; importing or correcting the earlier cacador-quiz English; any edit to questions/ or the extractor.
notes:
**DECISIONS** (epic-scoped log; durable record written to DESIGN.md § 9 in bead .1)

- D1 Translations are written fresh, one agent per group of chunk files, with both glossaries as READ FIRST; the earlier cacador-quiz English is never opened by a worker. Reason: a 39-question sample plus a tally of every species option found it wrong and inconsistent on species (arrabio→teal, pato-trombeteiro→wigeon and goldeneye, narceja-galega→great snipe) and on terms (de salto→jump method, jump hunting, walk-up); fixing it costs as much as redoing it and keeps its anchoring. Record: cac-qgb notes FOUND.
- D2 glossary/species.json holds every species name the bank uses, each surface form (singular and plural) its own entry, plus every species of Portaria 67/2024 (diariodarepublica.pt/dr/detalhe/portaria/67-2024-853384722). group is the manifest topic slug when the species' family has one (patos for every duck, tordos for every thrush, pombos-rolas for pigeons and doves), nao-cinegeticas for a protected species, outras-cinegeticas for a game species with no topic (corvids, starling, geese). Reason: rule 6 already enforces the shape and allows entries the bank never names (DESIGN.md § 4).
- D3 glossary/terms.json, shape { pt, en, note }, pt unique and in the bank's surface form, holds the hunting and legal vocabulary; the validator checks only its shape (new rule 7); its use in translations is checked by the meaning pass, not by a rule. Reason: terms inflect, a rule would be loose or noisy (cac-qgb D3).
- D4 Register is literal-leaning: keep the Portuguese order and structure where English allows, British spelling (licence, metres, colour), numbers, units and times as the Portuguese has them, a bare number or proper name copied unchanged. A Portuguese term with no English equivalent (montaria, listado, farropo, morouços, terçó) stays in Portuguese followed by the glossary's gloss in parentheses. Reason: the peek unblocks a word in the sentence being read; it is not a reading mode (DESIGN.md § 6, § 9 peek decision).
- D5 The meaning pass is a second agent, never the translator of the same file: reads pt and en side by side, rewrites en where it drifts or breaks a glossary or would make the keyed option wrong, flips status to checked, and writes notes only for an ambiguity it could not resolve; a fix it made goes in the bead's close reason, not in notes. Reason: notes are what a reviewer should know, not a change log (DESIGN.md § 3.3).
- D6 No hand review in this epic: every entry ends at checked; reviewed is flipped as Ross studies, through phase 4. Reason: cac-qgb D6.
- D7 en in the species glossary is the common name as British field guides print it, in its full form where one exists (Northern pintail, Eurasian wigeon, Common snipe, Jack snipe), capitalised as a name; the scientific name is as Portaria 67/2024 prints it, else the current IOC name. Precedent: the § 3.3 example (Northern pintail, Gadwall, Mallard). Rule 6 matches case-insensitively, so running text may lowercase it.
- D8 Translators leave status draft; only the meaning pass flips to checked, so rule 6 binds from the meaning pass on. Reason: DESIGN.md § 4 rule 6 skips draft; a translator's half-finished file must not fail lint.

title: Phase 4: the app
description:
Phase 4 of Caçador: the practice app, apps/web, built on the finished data package. One Portuguese question at a time with the English only while a button is held, a hint on request, a per-question history on the phone that brings recently wrong questions back sooner, 20-question 30-minute mock exams against 15 of 20, and progress by topic, section and hint pattern with a readiness score against 75 %.

WHO AND WHERE: Ross, as the one learner, on an Android Chrome phone installed from GitHub Pages (rosslote.github.io/cacador) and in a laptop browser. Installable, offline, static, no server, no account.

IN SCOPE: apps/web (Vite, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, react-router v7 library mode, shadcn/ui on Base UI, vitest with jsdom and Testing Library) and an e2e workspace (Playwright); Home, Practice with peek and hint, Exam, Progress with focused practice, Settings, Flagged; the IndexedDB storage module of DESIGN.md § 7 (answers, questionState, exams, flags) with localStorage `cacador.` for settings; export and import as one JSON file; web manifest, icons and a service worker; the GitHub Actions workflow that lints, tests, builds and deploys to Pages on push to main; English and pt-PT message files; DESIGN.md § 6 to § 9 updated with the decisions below; pnpm lint and pnpm test green.
OUT OF SCOPE: fixing a flagged translation or hint (a later bead reads the pasted Flagged list; none filed yet); text-to-speech, a vocabulary drill, a browse list of all 506 questions, links from a nudge's question number, accounts or sync, a custom domain (no epic owns these; none planned); any edit to questions/, the extractor or the loader.

D1 Public repo RossLote/cacador, GitHub Pages at the sub-path /cacador/ (Vite base, manifest start_url and scope, service worker scope, router basename), deployed by a workflow on push to main; the remote serves code and Pages only, beads stay as committed JSONL. Reason: a commit is the deploy and the repo gains a backup.
D2 Flags are local only: after answering, "English is off" and "Hint is off" taps with an optional one-line note; a Flagged page lists id, kind, note and stem with a Copy button (plain text, share sheet where available) and a tap to clear; flags travel in the export; the app writes nothing back and never sets status reviewed. Reason: no backend, nothing stored elsewhere, a page Ross can paste to an agent.
D3 Exam: free movement among the 20, answers changeable until Submit, auto-submit at 30:00, an interrupted exam resumes with the clock running from its start; no peek or hint in an exam; exam answers feed the weights. Reason: it runs as the real one does.
D4 Focused practice: a topic, section or pattern tapped in Progress starts a practice limited to it; the whole bank is the default. Reason: a weak topic is one tap from fixing.
D5 Readiness: per seen question the share right in its last three answers, unseen counting one third, averaged over 506 against 75 % with the unseen count beside it; draw weights wrong last time 4, unseen 3, streak 1 → 2, streak 2 → 1, streak 3+ → 0.5, no repeat within ten draws. Reason: rises only by covering and holding the bank.
D6 UI in English by default, pt-PT in settings, both message files. Reason: CLAUDE.md asks for both.
D7 Theme follows the system, light and dark, plain shadcn neutral, phone-first, no design canvas. Reason: no ceremony.
D8 Import merges answer records and rebuilds state; Clear progress behind a confirm. Reason: phone and laptop can both hold progress.
D9 Laptop: A/B/C or 1/2/3 answer, Enter advances, hold Space to peek. Reason: peek stays press-and-hold.
D10 Out: text-to-speech, vocabulary drill, nudge number links, accounts or sync. Reason: not in § 6, none blocks studying.
D11 Home: readiness, unseen count, Practice, Exam, Progress, Settings. Progress: accuracy by day, topic, section and pattern lists worst first with counts, past exams, Flagged. Reason: defaults accepted.
D12 Silent auto-update on next open; system fonts, no web fonts. Reason: no stale shell, offline fetches nothing.
D13 Playwright e2e workspace run by pnpm e2e, outside lint and test, as in Sumit. Reason: § 8 names it, gates stay fast.
D14 Each practice question shows section, topic and number; no browse list. Reason: nudges cite numbers; weighting covers browsing.
D15 The whole data package is bundled and cached, no lazy loading, loader unchanged. Reason: 109 KB gzipped in total.

DOES NOT: write to the data files or set reviewed; show English as a toggle; give feedback inside an exam; store anything off the device; add a server, an account or a Dolt remote; open the earlier cacador-quiz project.

NOTE FOR /epic: Sumit (/Users/ross.lote/Projects/personal/mathracer/mathracer, apps/web, e2e) is the precedent for every config file, the i18n store, the storage module shape and the manifest and icons; vite-plugin-pwa 2.0.0 clears minimumReleaseAge and supports Vite 8; react-router stays on 7 as Sumit pins it; the e2e webServer is vite preview with the base. The first bead amends DESIGN.md § 6 to § 9 (hosting, D2's amendment of the two § 9 lines that say reviewed is flipped through the app, the formulas of D5). The pt-PT messages file is content work. The remote origin is set and nothing is pushed; after the epic merges to main, git push -u origin main is the first deploy, and Pages must be enabled with GitHub Actions as the source (actions/configure-pages enablement, or once by hand in the repo settings). Scaffolding and config beads can run on Sonnet; the practice, exam and progress logic and the two formulas on Opus.

PROBLEM

Finding: For an imported exam whose questionIds is not 20 long, Past exams shows the score out of EXAM_SIZE (20) while the results page shows it out of exam.questionIds.length. The same exam gets two different denominators.

Failure scenario: apps/web/src/storage/exportFile.ts:95: An imported export holding a finished exam with 5 questionIds and score 5 is accepted. Progress > Past exams shows '5 out of 20, Not passed' (PastExams.tsx:35,39 with EXAM_SIZE), while its results page shows '5 out of 5' (ExamResultsPage.tsx:62 with questionIds.length) and still 'Not passed' (examPassed: 5 < 15). An exam with score 18 but answers that scoreExam rates 3 shows 'Passed' on the results page with 17 questions listed as wrong.
apps/web/src/exam/ExamResultsPage.tsx:62: Import a version 1 export with an exam whose questionIds has 19 entries (readExam checks only that it is a list of positive integers) and score 15. Progress → Past exams shows '15 / 20' and an aria-label of '15 of 20'. Tapping the row opens /exam/results/<id>, which shows '15 out of 19'. Both screens apply examPassed(15) and say Passed. One exam gets two denominators depending on the screen, and DESIGN § 6.5 and § 6.6 both say 'out of 20'.
apps/web/src/progress/PastExams.tsx:35: Import accepts an exam with any number of question ids (readExam only checks that each id is a positive integer) and any non-negative score. Import a file holding a finished exam with 10 questionIds and score 9. Progress shows the row as '9 / 20' with the aria-label '…: 9 of 20, Not passed'. Tapping it opens /exam/results/<id>, where ScorePanel shows '9 out of 10'. The two screens report different totals for one exam.

Root cause: readExam accepts a questionIds list of any length, and PastExams and ExamResultsPage take the exam size from two different sources.

Skeptics:
- confirmed: Confirmed. An imported version 1 export can contain a finished exam whose questionIds list has a length other than 20, because readExam (exportFile.ts:95) only checks each id.
